skill.name: frontend-dev-guidelines
skill.description: Frontend development guidelines for React and TypeScript applications using Suspense, TanStack Query, TanStack Router, MUI v7, feature folders, and performance patterns.
skill.summary: Guides React and TypeScript frontend development with modern component, routing, data fetching, styling, and performance patterns.
skill.author: Dimon94

security_audit.summary: The static findings were reviewed against the skill files and are false positives from Markdown documentation and fixed frontend examples. The dynamic imports are React code-splitting examples, path traversal detections are import paths or documentation links, and network references are local application API client guidance. No prompt injection, malicious intent, data exfiltration, or executable installer behavior was found.

content.value_statement: Frontend teams need consistent patterns for React, TypeScript, routing, data fetching, and loading states. This skill provides practical guidelines and examples for building maintainable frontend features.
actual_capabilities: Guides new React components using TypeScript props, hooks, default exports, and Suspense boundaries.
Shows TanStack Query patterns with useSuspenseQuery, cache-first reads, mutations, and invalidation.
Explains feature folder organization for API services, components, hooks, helpers, types, and routes.
Documents TanStack Router patterns with lazy loaded route components and breadcrumb loaders.
Provides MUI v7 styling guidance for sx props, typed style objects, and Grid size syntax.
Covers frontend performance practices such as memoization, debouncing, cleanup, and dynamic imports.
limitations: The guidance assumes a React, TypeScript, MUI, TanStack Query, and TanStack Router stack.
It does not provide runnable generators, scripts, or automated migrations.
Project-specific aliases and API routes must be adapted to the user repository.
Examples are documentation patterns and may need updates for different library versions.

use_cases.title: Create a Feature Module
use_cases.description: Plan a new feature folder with API services, components, hooks, helpers, types, and route files.

use_cases.title: Standardize Team Patterns
use_cases.description: Review component, routing, styling, and data fetching choices against a shared frontend convention.

use_cases.title: Modernize Legacy Screens
use_cases.description: Refactor older loading, query, and layout patterns toward Suspense, typed services, and stable layouts.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Component
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a React TypeScript component for [purpose]. Follow the frontend guidelines for props, hooks, exports, MUI styling, and Suspense boundaries when needed.

prompt_templates.title: Add Data Fetching
prompt_templates.prompt: Add TanStack Query data fetching for [entity]. Use useSuspenseQuery, a feature API service, typed return values, cache keys, and the project loading pattern.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Routed Feature
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a complete feature for [workflow]. Include folder structure, route file, lazy loading, API service, types, components, and user notifications.

prompt_templates.title: Review Frontend Architecture
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this frontend code for guideline compliance. Focus on file organization, Suspense usage, cache strategy, MUI v7 syntax, performance, and TypeScript standards.

output_examples.input: Create a user details page with data loading and edit feedback.
output_examples.output: A feature plan with route placement, typed API service methods, a Suspense wrapped component, mutation flow, snackbar feedback, and cache invalidation steps.

output_examples.input: Review a dashboard component that fetches several datasets.
output_examples.output: A concise review covering query placement, parallel data loading, memoization needs, layout stability, MUI Grid syntax, and cleanup recommendations.

output_examples.input: Organize a new posts feature in an existing React app.
output_examples.output: A folder outline with API, components, hooks, helpers, types, public exports, route files, and import alias guidance.

best_practices: Use Suspense boundaries and useSuspenseQuery for new data driven components.
Keep domain code inside feature folders and export only the public feature API.
Use typed MUI sx styles, MUI v7 Grid syntax, and stable loading layouts.
anti_patterns: Returning early with standalone loading spinners that shift the layout.
Creating deep relative imports when project aliases can express intent clearly.
Mixing feature-specific components into shared component folders without reuse needs.

faq.question: What frontend stack does this skill target?
faq.answer: It targets React with TypeScript, MUI v7, TanStack Query, TanStack Router, and project import aliases.

faq.question: Can it create complete feature structures?
faq.answer: Yes. It can guide folder layout, route placement, API services, types, hooks, and component organization.

faq.question: Does it run code or install packages?
faq.answer: No. The skill is documentation and examples. It does not include executable scripts or package installation commands.

faq.question: How does it handle loading states?
faq.answer: It recommends SuspenseLoader and useSuspenseQuery for new components to keep layouts stable.

faq.question: Is it useful for legacy code?
faq.answer: Yes. It can identify older loading, query, import, and styling patterns that should be modernized.

faq.question: Will examples match every repository?
faq.answer: No. API routes, aliases, and folder names may need adaptation for each project.
